blocks.raw: # Products
blocks.text: Products

blocks.raw: Create and manage your organization's SKUs, Brands, Categories, Attributes, Labels, and Collections from a single self-serve Products page.
blocks.text: Create and manage your organization's SKUs, Brands, Categories, Attributes, Labels, and Collections from a single self-serve Products page.

blocks.raw: A **Product** is an item your organization sells. You can add each product to the catalog with details such as its name, description, brand, category, price, and other characteristics.
blocks.text: A Product is an item your organization sells. You can add each product to the catalog with details such as its name, description, brand, category, price, and other characteristics.

blocks.raw: A product can be identified by a **SKU**, described using a **Brand**, **Category**, and **Attributes**, and organized using **Labels** and **Collections**. See the <Anchor target="_blank" href="https://docs.capillarytech.com/docs/product-entities-management#key-terms">Key terms</Anchor> section below to understand how each of these terms relates to a product.
blocks.text: A product can be identified by a SKU, described using a Brand, Category, and Attributes, and organized using Labels and Collections. See the Key terms section below to understand how each of these terms relates to a product.

blocks.raw: ## Key terms
blocks.text: Key terms

blocks.raw:
| **Term** | **Description** | | ------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | **[SKU (Stock Keeping Unit)](#creating-and-editing-a-sku)** | A SKU is the unique code used to identify a specific version of a product.

For example, a blue shirt in size Medium and the same shirt in size Large are treated as two different SKUs. Each SKU represents one distinct version of a product and helps you track pricing, inventory, and variations accurately.

Every product in the system must have a unique SKU. | | **[Brand](#creating-and-editing-a-brand)** | A brand represents the name or label associated with a product, such as Nike, Adidas, or Apple. Brands help you group products by manufacturer or label, and support reporting and organization. A brand can also be nested under a parent brand, for example, a sub-brand under its parent company.

For example, Nike can be the parent brand, with Jordan as its sub-brand. | | **[Category](#creating-and-editing-a-category)** | A category groups similar products together. Categories help you organize products and make them easier to search, filter, and report on. Categories support a parent-child hierarchy, so you can nest related categories under a broader one.

For example, Apparel can be the parent category, with Shirts, Trousers, and Jackets as child categories. | | **[Attribute](#creating-an-attribute)** | An attribute describes a characteristic of a product, such as Colour, Size, or Material. Attributes let you capture consistent, structured details about a SKU instead of free-text notes,

For example, a T-shirt SKU can have the attributes Colour = Red, Size = Medium, and Material = Cotton. | | **[Label](#creating-a-label)** | A label is a tag you attach to a SKU to categorize or filter it. A label can have an expiry, so it automatically stops applying to a SKU after a set time instead of needing manual removal.

For example, you can assign the label "Summer Sale" to selected SKUs with an expiry date of 31 August. After that date, the label is automatically removed from those SKUs. | | **[Collection](#grouping-products-dynamically-collections)** | A collection is a saved, rule-based group of SKUs. Unlike a manually maintained list, a collection's membership recalculates automatically on a schedule, so it always reflects which SKUs currently match its rules.

For example, you can create a collection that includes all SKUs in the Footwear category priced under 5,000. When a new footwear SKU is added with a price below 5,000, it is automatically included in the collection. |

rows: A SKU is the unique code used to identify a specific version of a product.For example, a blue shirt in size Medium and the same shirt in size Large are treated as two different SKUs. Each SKU represents one distinct version of a product and helps you track pricing, inventory, and variations accurately.Every product in the system must have a unique SKU.

A brand represents the name or label associated with a product, such as Nike, Adidas, or Apple. Brands help you group products by manufacturer or label, and support reporting and organization. A brand can also be nested under a parent brand, for example, a sub-brand under its parent company.For example, Nike can be the parent brand, with Jordan as its sub-brand.

A category groups similar products together. Categories help you organize products and make them easier to search, filter, and report on. Categories support a parent-child hierarchy, so you can nest related categories under a broader one. For example, Apparel can be the parent category, with Shirts, Trousers, and Jackets as child categories.

An attribute describes a characteristic of a product, such as Colour, Size, or Material. Attributes let you capture consistent, structured details about a SKU instead of free-text notes, For example, a T-shirt SKU can have the attributes Colour = Red, Size = Medium, and Material = Cotton.

A label is a tag you attach to a SKU to categorize or filter it. A label can have an expiry, so it automatically stops applying to a SKU after a set time instead of needing manual removal.For example, you can assign the label "Summer Sale" to selected SKUs with an expiry date of 31 August. After that date, the label is automatically removed from those SKUs.

A collection is a saved, rule-based group of SKUs. Unlike a manually maintained list, a collection's membership recalculates automatically on a schedule, so it always reflects which SKUs currently match its rules. For example, you can create a collection that includes all SKUs in the Footwear category priced under 5,000. When a new footwear SKU is added with a price below 5,000, it is automatically included in the collection.

blocks.raw: ## Creating a SKU
blocks.text: Creating a SKU

blocks.raw: To create a SKU, follow these steps:
blocks.text: To create a SKU, follow these steps:

blocks.raw:
1. Navigate to **Entities** > **Products** > **SKUs**. 2. Select **+ New Product**. 3. Enter the **SKU code**, **Product name**, and **Description** (all required). 4. (Optional) Select **+ Add label**.

i. Select an existing label from the **Label name** dropdown, or select **+ New label**.

ii. If you select **+ New label**, a modal appears. Enter the label details.

iii. Select **Expiry configuration** to define how long the label remains assigned to the product. If no expiry is configured, the label assignment defaults to **Never Expire**.

iv. Select **Add Label**. The label is created and becomes available in the **Label name** dropdown.

blocks.raw: ### Viewing and editing a SKU
blocks.text: Viewing and editing a SKU

blocks.raw: To view or edit a SKU, follow these steps:
blocks.text: To view or edit a SKU, follow these steps:

blocks.raw:
1. Navigate to **Entities** > **Products** > **SKUs**.
2. On the SKUs list, review each product's **Product name** and **SKU code**, **Labels**, **Brand**, **Category**, and when it was last updated. Select the **Product** **Name **column header to sort the SKU code alphabetically. Use **Search by code** to find a specific SKU.
3. Select a SKU to open its detail page, showing everything you set when creating it.
4. Select **Edit** to change any field, then select **Update product**.

   **Note:** The **SKU code** can't be changed after the SKU is created.

blocks.raw: ## Creating a label
blocks.text: Creating a label

blocks.raw: Labels let you tag SKUs for filtering and reporting, with an optional expiry.
blocks.text: Labels let you tag SKUs for filtering and reporting, with an optional expiry.

blocks.raw: To create a label, follow these steps:
blocks.text: To create a label, follow these steps:

blocks.raw:
1. Navigate to **Entities** > **Products** > **Labels**.
2. Select **+ Create Label**.
3. Enter an **External ID** and **Label Name** (both required), and an optional **Description**.
4. Set an **Expiry Configuration**:

   | Option                         | Behavior                                                   |
   | ------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
   | Never Expire                   | The label stays on the SKU indefinitely.                   |
   | Fixed Date                     | You choose a specific calendar date for it to expire.      |
   | Expire after X days            | The label expires a set number of days after it's applied. |
   | Expire at end of current month | The label expires on the last day of the current month.    |
   | Expire at end of current year  | The label expires on the last day of the current year.     |
5. Select **Add Label**.

blocks.raw: ## Grouping products dynamically (collections)
blocks.text: Grouping products dynamically (collections)

blocks.raw: Collections are rule-based groups of SKUs that stay up to date automatically, instead of a static list you maintain by hand, for example, "all SKUs in the Footwear category priced under 5,000."
blocks.text: Collections are rule-based groups of SKUs that stay up to date automatically, instead of a static list you maintain by hand, for example, "all SKUs in the Footwear category priced under 5,000."

blocks.raw: To create a collection, follow these steps:
blocks.text: To create a collection, follow these steps:

blocks.raw:
1. Go to **Entities** > **Products** > **Collections**.
2. Select **+ Create Collection**.
3. Enter a **Collection name** and, optionally, an **External ID** and **Description**.
4. Choose how often membership recalculates under **Refresh frequency**.
5. Under **Membership criteria**, choose whether condition blocks must all match (**AND**) or whether any can match (**OR**). Within each block, select **+ Add condition** to add an attribute, operator, and value. Select **+ Add condition block** to add another block.
6. Select **Save collection**.
